subject: Onboarding: Performance tuning plan for Acme - model routing & quant profiles
messages:
From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Torres <elaine@acme-corp.com>, Rajesh Gupta <rajesh@acme-corp.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Handoff: Acme onboarding + early perf tuning items

Hi Elaine / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the productive kickoff last week. Per our conversation I’m looping in Monica (CSM) and Connor (SRE) to start the operational handoff and to outline a short tuning sprint we recommend during the first two onboarding weeks. Attached is a lightweight checklist to kick things off.

High-level asks for your team before our sync on Thursday:
- Confirm the production peak QPS and 95th pct latency target for customer-facing endpoints.
- Confirm whether you’ll use our hosted API initially or expect Dedicated capacity within 30 days.
- Share a sample of typical prompt length distributions (avg tokens / 95th pct).

What we'll cover in the tuning sprint (two-week cadence):
1) Model selection & quant profile recommendation (q8_0 vs q4_0 tradeoffs).
2) Batching strategy and dynamic batching config tuned to your P95 and P99 SLOs.
3) KV/prefix caching for chat flows and common system prompts.
4) Routing policy setup — latency-first route with cost fallback + canary routes to Dedicated if configured.

Attachments: onboarding-tuning-checklist.xlsx, acme-infra-mapping.json

Monica — can you propose a 60-minute working session this Thu/ Fri to run through the checklist and pick the initial quant profile?

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Handoff: Acme onboarding + early perf tuning items

Hi Elaine / Rajesh — thanks Dylan. I’m Monica, your CSM — I’ll run the operational plan and own the tuning sprint. I pulled together an initial implementation plan (see bullets below) and attached a short primer on quant profile tradeoffs.

Implementation / tuning plan (week 0–2):
- Week 0 (prep): collect metrics, prompt samples, infra mapping (we have acme-infra-mapping.json). Confirm hosted vs Dedicated decision.
- Week 1 (baseline + config): run a baseline load on hosted with synthetic traffic, enable dynamic batching with a 50ms aggregation window (start conservative), and apply q8_0 for non-sensitive generation paths.
- Week 2 (opt + rollouts): evaluate P95/P99 latency impact; where cost matters we try q4_0 for non-critical endpoints and measure hallucination/regression on your prompt set. If Dedicated is requested, plan a canary route: 10% traffic to Dedicated variant for 24–48 hrs, monitor token cost and latency.

Key technical questions — please confirm before our call:
- Peak sustained QPS and burst QPS observed in production (or expected).
- Typical prompt length (tokens) and fraction of chat vs one-shot completion traffic.
- Any regulatory constraint requiring private deployment / in-region only.
- Whether you want prefix caching for system prompts (most customers see 20–40% token reduction).

On quant profiles: we recommend starting with q8_0 on critical paths where quality matters; trial q4_0 on lower-impact routes. I attached initial-quant-profiles.pdf with observed latency/cost deltas on our 8-bit and 4-bit profiles.

Proposed working session: Thu Jun 18, 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri Jun 19, 09:00–10:00 PT — which works?

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
--
Monica Patel
monica.patel@redwood.com
From: Elaine Torres <elaine@acme-corp.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: Acme onboarding + early perf tuning items

Monica — thanks and good to meet you both. Quick answers while I gather the metrics: 

- Peak sustained QPS: ~80 qps during business hours, occasional bursts to ~220 qps.
- Target P95 latency target: <= 250 ms for customer-facing chat.
- Prompt profile: average ~120 tokens, 95th pct ~420 tokens; about 65% chat (multi-turn), 35% one-shot.
- We plan to start on hosted API for the first 4–6 weeks and re-evaluate Dedicated after seeing cost curves.
- We want prefix caching enabled for the chat system prompts if Redwood supports partial prefix reuse.

A couple of questions:
1) For dynamic batching, will the 50ms aggregation window add to our P95? If so, what is the observed delta for similar customers?
2) For q4_0 we are worried about subtle quality regressions — how do you recommend we validate quality during the trial?

Attaching a sanitized traffic sample (redacted) — hope this helps.

On Thu Jun 18, 09:00 AM, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Monica here — I’ll confirm the calendar after I hear from Elaine.

Thanks,
Elaine

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: Acme onboarding + early perf tuning items

Thanks for the quick responses, Elaine — this is perfect context. Quick notes and next steps (confirming our Thu -> moved to Mon cadence):

1) Meeting: I booked a working session for Mon Jun 22, 11:00–12:00 PT (invite sent). Goal: agree on baseline test, quant profile for each route, and batching window for the first A/B.

2) Dynamic batching latency impact: 50ms aggregation commonly adds ~10–40ms to median but can add up to ~60–80ms in low-util periods. We’ll start with 50ms but configure adaptive thresholds so the runtime reduces batching under low QPS to protect tail latency. We’ll measure end-to-end P95 in the baseline run so you can see the delta.

3) Validating q4_0 quality: we’ll run a paired-eval harness against your prompt set (we use a small MAPE/acceptance test plus human spot checks). If we see >3% user-facing regression on key prompt families we’ll rollback the route or restrict q4_0 to low-impact endpoints.

4) Prefix caching: Redwood supports segment-level prefix reuse (partial KV cache). For multi-turn chat we generally see 20–40% token savings — we’ll instrument cost delta in the baseline.

5) Routing policy: propose a primary latency-first route to hosted q8_0 model, with a cost-fallback route to q4_0 for batchable, non-critical endpoints. If you enable Dedicated later, we’ll add a canary route at 10% traffic. We’ll include automatic fallback if latency exceeds your P95 target.

6) Pre-call asks (please upload before Mon):
- Redacted traffic sample (you already sent one)
- Any restricted prompts flagged for higher-quality path
- Confirmation of SLO tradeoffs (e.g., P95 target vs acceptable cost increase)

Attachments: initial-quant-profiles.pdf

I’ll own the runbook items and Connor will be on the call to validate the baseline load harness. Looking forward — we’ll bring a short decision matrix and a rollback playbook.

Cheers,
Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
